All Out for our first bargaining session 2-15-23!

The current 2020 agreement between Brown and the Graduate Labor Organization (GLO) expires on June 30, 2023, and we have been at the bargaining table since February seeking agreement on a new contract. Unfortunately, we remain very far apart on core issues, and there is no expectation that a successor agreement or an extension will be in place by the expiration date later this week.

The Graduate Labor Organization and the University reached an agreement on stipends and discrimination and harassment clauses in their new contract at a meeting last Wednesday — a major breakthrough in negotiations, which began in February.

Voting is live on the Tentative Agreement for our next contract! Now it’s up to all of us to vote to ratify this contract and make it official. Our ratification vote is open through midnight on Monday, December 18th.

When negotiations began in February, GLO proposed a 12% base stipend increase for fiscal year 2027, resulting in a stipend of $58,462. The union also proposed another 11% stipend increase in FY28 and a 10% increase in FY29.
The University countered GLO’s proposal by offering a 6.7% stipend increase over five years
They are currently proposing a 0% raise for next year along with raises in subsequent years that fall well below historical averages for inflation.

About two weeks later, the University declined to voluntarily recognize graduate fellows.

Graduate student TAs and AIs are entitled to receive a TRB if they meet eligibility requirements.
For half-time appointments (20 hours/week) or more, the TRB provides 9 credit hours of resident (in-state) tuition.
For appointments between 10 and 19 hours/week, the TRB provides ½ of the 9- hour resident tuition amount.
For half-time appointments (20 hours/week) or more, the TRB provides 3 credit hours of resident (in-state) tuition.
Graduate student GRAs are not entitled to receive a TRB if they meet eligibility requirements. TRB awards are approved by the student’s department based on funding availability.

An Academic Graduate Student (AGS) employee is benefits-eligible if expected to work in one or a combination of AGS titles for at least 20 SWH and for at least 4.5 months (135 calendar days).

It is required that departments hiring benefits-eligible GRAs will cover the cost of the graduate student’s tuition, or the relevant proportion of the tuition when a student has simultaneous benefits-eligible TA/AI and GRA employment.
UT provides all eligible AGS employees with 100% premium support for UT SHIP, also known as AcademicBlue.
All benefits eligible AGS employees enrolled during the summer will continue to receive 100% premium support for their coverage

UT Austin also provides 50% premium support for dependent coverage, with AGS employees paying the remaining 50% of their dependent premiums directly to Academic HealthPlans, the plan administrator, monthly.

Part-time (20-29 SWH) AGS employees will receive 50% premium sharing for UT SELECT and 25% premium sharing for dependent coverage. Full-time (30+ SWH) AGS employees will receive 100% premium sharing for UT SELECT and 50% premium sharing for dependent coverage.
